title: RAG in 2025: State of the Art and the Road Forward — Tengyu Ma, MongoDB (acq. Voyage AI)
talk_summary: Tengyu Ma (Voyage AI/MongoDB) argues RAG beats long-context and fine-tuning for cost and modularity, and surveys retrieval improvements: better embedding models, hybrid search + rerankers, query decomposition, document enrichment, domain-specific and fine-tuned embeddings, matryoshka/quantized vectors, and multimodal embeddings. Most of the talk is vendor framing; the transferable parts are chunk-enrichment and retrieval-cost mechanics.

takeaways.what_they_do: When chunking long documents, prepend global info (title, headers, category, author, date, or LLM-generated context) to each chunk so it stays searchable after truncation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to add the global information into each of the trunks and some of this global information can be added by large language models

takeaways.technique: Retrieve small units, not whole documents
takeaways.what_they_do: Even when a long document fits in context, retrieve at paragraph/page granularity because feeding 100k tokens per query is expensive and models miss mid-context details.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you give 100k uh tokens to large model every time you answer any question if you do some cost analysis you'll find that that core is very very expensive
takeaways.numbers: 100k-token document per query called 'very very expensive'

takeaways.what_they_do: Use an LLM to lengthen or split the query into sub-queries, then search each against different document subsets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also decompose the longer query to small subqueries so that you can have like a few different queries and search for different subset of documents

takeaways.what_they_do: Truncate high-dim embeddings to a prefix or lower precision with small accuracy loss, cutting vector storage up to ~10-100x.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can save you know 100x you know at least 10x without losing much
takeaways.numbers: ~10x savings with little loss; ~100x costs ~5-10% accuracy

takeaways.technique: Hybrid search + reranker for review context
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine lexical (keyword) search with vector search, then rerank the merged candidates with a reranker model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use you know lexical search and other kind of search and then combine them with a reancher
